fullPassage:
(A) Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! How about staying a little longer? We can work on some drills — just the two of us." Eva hesitated. "I don't know, Coach. I'm pretty tired." Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile. "Just ten minutes. It'll be fun. I promise." Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed reluctant. They practiced passing the ball together.

(B) The next game, Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva played. There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score but led the team successfully. After the game she ran over, saying, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had it in you. I'm just here to remind you of that." Eva's face softened, as she realized she had been too hard on herself. She said to herself, "What matters is doing my best, not being perfect."

(C) Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. She suggested, "You don't have to be perfect. Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion. And you've always had plenty of that." Eva's gaze met Ms. Blake's. "Do you really think so?" Ms. Blake said firmly, "Yes. The way you play, the energy you bring — that's what makes you special. Not the goals scored or the trophies won. It's the love you have for the game." Eva nodded thoughtfully.

(D) Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed elsewhere. Breaking the silence, Ms. Blake asked, "Do you remember the final game last year?" "Yeah, I remember." Eva recalled the game where she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so worried I can't score a goal or even pass the ball properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes," said Eva.

questions.passage: Eva agreed, though she still seemed (A)[reluctant / eager]. The next game, there was a new (B)[confidence / anxiety] that hadn't been there before. Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about (C)[passion / competition].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Eva는 여전히 꺼려하는(reluctant) 듯했고, 새로운 자신감(confidence)이 있었으며, 축구는 열정(passion)에 관한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reluctant — confidence — passion: 원문 일치.
❌ ② eager(열망하는): reluctant의 반의어.
❌ ③ anxiety(불안): confidence의 반의어.
❌ ④ competition(경쟁): 원문은 passion.
det.tip: reluctant(꺼리는)↔eager(열망), confidence(자신감)↔anxiety(불안), passion(열정)

questions.passage: Ms. Blake placed a (A)[reassuring / threatening] hand on Eva's shoulder. Eva's gaze (B)[met / avoided] Ms. Blake's. Eva's face (C)[softened / hardened], as she realized she had been too hard on herself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Ms. Blake가 안심시키는(reassuring) 손을 올렸고, Eva의 시선이 마주쳤고(met), 표정이 부드러워졌다(softened).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ reassuring — met — softened: 원문 일치.
❌ ① avoided(피했다): met의 반의어.
❌ ② threatening(위협적): reassuring의 반의어.
❌ ④ hardened(굳어짐): softened의 반의어.
det.tip: reassuring(안심시키는)↔threatening(위협적), met(마주쳤다)↔avoided(피했다), softened↔hardened

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were (A)[slow / swift] and her focus seemed elsewhere. Eva recalled the game where she scored three goals. det.analysis:
✅ ② slow — good — firmly: 원문 일치.
❌ ① swift(빠른): slow의 반의어.
❌ ③ terrible(끔찍한): good의 반의어.
❌ ④ hesitantly(망설이며): firmly의 반의어.
det.tip: slow(느린)↔swift(빠른), firmly(단호하게)↔hesitantly(망설이며)

det.analysis:
❌ ③ doubt → confidence: 원문은 'a new confidence'. doubt는 반대.
✅ ① smile: 원문 그대로.
❌ ② reluctant: 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ successfully: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: confidence(자신감)↔doubt(의심). 긍정적 변화의 흐름을 파악

questions.passage: Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a ①<u>reassuring</u> hand on Eva's shoulder. "Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about ②<u>passion</u>." Ms. Blake said ③<u>firmly</u>, "The way you play, the energy you bring — that's what makes you special." Eva nodded ④<u>carelessly</u>.

det.korean: Eva가 생각에 잠겨(thoughtfully) 고개를 끄덕였다. ④ carelessly(부주의하게)는 thoughtfully의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ carelessly → thoughtfully: 원문은 'nodded thoughtfully'. carelessly는 반대.
✅ ① reassuring: 원문 그대로.
❌ ② passion: 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ firmly: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: thoughtfully(생각에 잠겨)↔carelessly(부주의하게). 부사의 뉘앙스 구별

det.korean: 자신에게 너무 엄격했다(hard). ④ lenient(관대한)는 hard의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ lenient → hard: 원문은 'too hard on herself'. lenient(관대한)은 반대.
✅ ① hesitated: 원문 그대로.
❌ ② elsewhere: 원문 그대로.

det.tip: hard on oneself(자신에게 엄격한)↔lenient(관대한). be too hard on = ~에게 너무 엄격하다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment, then called out. Eva hesitated. Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile. Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ reluctant(꺼리는): 원문 일치. hesitated 후에도 여전히 꺼림.
❌ ① enthusiastic(열정적): 꺼리는 것과 반대.
❌ ② confident(자신감 있는): 아직 자신감이 없는 상태.
❌ ③ delighted(기쁜): 맥락과 반대.
det.tip: reluctant = 꺼리는, 마지못한. agree but seem reluctant = 동의했지만 마지못해

questions.passage: Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. She suggested that soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion. Eva's gaze met Ms. Blake's. Ms. Blake said firmly that Eva's energy and love for the game make her special. Eva nodded __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① thoughtfully: 원문 일치. 코치의 말을 곱씹으며 고개를 끄덕임.
❌ ② angrily(화나서): 맥락과 반대.
❌ ③ indifferently(무관심하게): Eva가 깊이 생각 중.
❌ ④ hastily(성급하게): 깊이 생각하는 것과 반대.
det.tip: thoughtfully = 사려 깊게, 생각에 잠겨. nod thoughtfully = 곱씹으며 끄덕이다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and her focus seemed elsewhere. She asked about the final game last year. Eva recalled scoring three goals. Now she was worried she couldn't even pass the ball properly. Eva was afraid of making mistakes. Ms. Blake responded by saying Eva didn't have to be __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Ms. Blake는 Eva가 완벽할(perfect) 필요가 없다고 말했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② perfect: 원문 'You don't have to be perfect'. 핵심 메시지.
❌ ① successful: 원문의 핵심이 아님.
❌ ③ popular: 맥락과 무관.
❌ ④ talented: 재능이 아닌 완벽주의가 주제.
det.tip: You don't have to be perfect = 완벽할 필요 없다. 글의 핵심 메시지

questions.passage: Eva <u>hesitated</u>. "I don't know, Coach. I'm pretty tired."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 hesitated와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ wavered(주저하다): hesitated의 동의어.
❌ ① refused(거절하다): 완전히 거절한 것이 아님.
❌ ② agreed(동의하다): 아직 동의하지 않은 상태.
❌ ④ insisted(고집하다): 반대 방향.
det.tip: hesitate(망설이다) = waver, falter, pause. ↔ decide firmly

questions.passage: Ms. Blake said <u>firmly</u>, "Yes. The way you play, the energy you bring — that's what makes you special."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 firmly와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② decisively(단호하게): firmly의 동의어.
❌ ① quietly(조용히): 확신의 강도가 다름.
❌ ③ casually(가볍게): firmly와 반대 뉘앙스.
❌ ④ nervously(긴장하여): 단호함과 반대.
det.tip: firmly(단호하게) = decisively, resolutely. ↔ hesitantly, nervously

questions.passage: Eva's face <u>softened</u>, as she realized she had been too hard on herself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 softened와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ relaxed(편안해지다): softened의 동의어. 긴장이 풀림.
❌ ① tightened(굳어지다): softened의 반의어.
❌ ② brightened(밝아지다): 유사하지만 softened은 긴장 완화.
❌ ③ froze(얼어붙다): softened의 반의어.
det.tip: softened(부드러워지다) = relaxed, eased. ↔ hardened, tightened

questions.passage: Eva agreed, though she still seemed <u>reluctant</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 reluctant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① willing(기꺼이 하는): reluctant의 반의어.
❌ ② hesitant(망설이는): reluctant과 유사.
❌ ③ uncertain(불확실한): reluctant과 유사.
❌ ④ cautious(조심스러운): reluctant과 유사.
det.tip: reluctant(꺼리는)↔willing(기꺼이). be reluctant to = ~하기를 꺼리다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake placed a <u>reassuring</u> hand on Eva's shoulder.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 reassuring과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ alarming(불안하게 하는): reassuring의 반의어.
❌ ① comforting(위로하는): reassuring과 동의어.
❌ ② encouraging(격려하는): reassuring과 유사.
❌ ④ soothing(진정시키는): reassuring과 동의어.
det.tip: reassuring(안심시키는)↔alarming(불안하게 하는). reassure = re(다시)+assure(확신시키다)

questions.passage:
(A) Eva recalled the <u>game</u> where she scored three goals. She was quite good back then. It was the final match of the season.
(B) The children were playing a board <u>game</u> in the living room. They laughed and chatted all afternoon. It was a relaxing way to spend the weekend.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 game의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ 경기 – 오락: (A)는 축구 경기(scored goals), (B)는 보드게임(오락).
❌ ① 오락 – 경기: 의미 뒤바뀜.
❌ ② 경기 – 경기: (B)는 경기가 아닌 오락.
❌ ③ 오락 – 오락: (A)는 축구 경기.
det.tip: game: ① 경기(sports), ② 오락/게임(board game), ③ 사냥감(wild game)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a strong feeling of enthusiasm or excitement for something"

det.analysis:
✅ ② passion(열정): 정의와 일치.
❌ ① perfection(완벽): 열정이 아님.
❌ ③ patience(인내): 열정과 다름.
❌ ④ precision(정밀함): 열정과 무관.
det.tip: passion = 열정, 격정. Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion.

questions.passage: The next game, Eva didn't score but led the team __________. (successful) Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva played with new confidence. After the game she ran over, saying thanks.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.analysis: ✅ successfully: led(동사)를 수식하는 부사가 필요. successful(형용사)→successfully(부사).
det.tip: successful(형용사: 성공적인) → successfully(부사: 성공적으로). 동사 수식 = 부사

questions.passage: Eva nodded __________. She realized the importance of the coach's words. (thoughtful)
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.analysis: ✅ thoughtfully: nodded(동사)를 수식하는 부사. thoughtful(형)→thoughtfully(부사).
det.tip: thoughtful(형용사: 사려 깊은) → thoughtfully(부사: 사려 깊게). -ful → -fully

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed Eva's slow movements and lack of focus. She asked about last year's final game. Eva remembered scoring three goals. But now she was afraid of making mistakes. Ms. Blake told her she didn't have to be perfect. She said soccer is about __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: passion and love for the game

det.korean: 축구는 열정과 경기에 대한 사랑(passion and love)에 관한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ passion and love for the game: 원문 'it's about passion' + 'the love you have for the game'.
❌ ① winning trophies: 원문은 'Not the goals scored or the trophies won'으로 부정.
❌ ② practicing drills: 부분적이지 핵심이 아님.
❌ ③ avoiding mistakes: 반대. 실수를 두려워하지 말라는 메시지.
det.tip: Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion. 핵심 메시지 파악

ch: she needed to practice harder to score more goals
she had been too hard on herself and doing her best mattered most
the coach was wrong about her abilities
she should quit soccer and find a different sport

det.korean: Eva는 자신에게 너무 엄격했으며 최선을 다하는 것이 가장 중요하다는 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문 'too hard on herself' + 'What matters is doing my best, not being perfect'.
❌ ① 더 열심히 연습: 글의 메시지와 반대.
❌ ③ 코치가 틀렸다: 글에서 코치에게 감사함.
❌ ④ 축구를 그만두다: 글의 방향과 완전히 반대.
det.tip: be too hard on oneself = 자신에게 너무 엄격하다. What matters is doing my best = 최선이 중요
